patch_description: The current program optimizes only soft (log-sum-exp) approximations of min/max squared distances, which plateau near the reference ratio (~0.240). Two targeted improvements: (1) add a final L-BFGS-B polish directly on the true objective -(dmin^2/dmax^2) with an analytic gradient (the exact gradient is cheap: only the argmin and argmax pairs contribute), applied after the soft sharpening stages, which squeezes out extra precision the soft objective cannot reach; (2) diversify the structured starts by placing the two extra points along different axes (z, x, y) of the icosahedron, since the icosahedron+poles family is the most promising basin. Keep trial count at 10 to avoid increasing the already-high eval time; the polish is fast because it involves only a few active pairs.
